signals.text: Compassion, respect and a sense of global responsibility are woven into daily school life, helping our children grow into thoughtful, caring citizens of the wider world.
Our beautiful rural setting provides rich opportunities for outdoor learning, reflection and exploration, and our strong Christian ethos underpins our commitment to inclusion, kindness and community.
At Kilmersdon, our children flourish within a close-knit community built on our core values of Peace, Perseverance, Forgiveness, Trust, Friendship and Hope.

Pupils are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is "right" and "wrong", all people living in England are subject to its law.

pageCache.pageTitle: Kilmersdon Church School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our vision and values are at the core of everything we do. They underpin our teaching and learning, and provide an environment which prepares our pupils as confident, happy citizens.
Our Vision Statement
At Kilmersdon Church School, we create a place of trust, forgiveness and peace so that our children can develop the skills they need to persevere and flourish in life. With friendship and hope, all our children are able to live life in all its fullness.
Our Christian Values
Friendship, Perseverance, Trust, Peace, Forgiveness and Hope.
Values
Find out more about our values - click below
Autumn Term 1 FRIENDSHIP
Autumn Term 2 PERSEVERANCE
Spring Term 2 FORGIVENESS
We are proud to be part of the East Mendip Trinity Community (Holy Trinity Coleford, St Andrew’s Holcombe, St Peter and St Paul, KIlmersdon).
LINK TO EAST MENDIP TRINITY WEBSITE
Promoting Fundamental British Values
In accordance with The Department for Education we aim to actively promote British values in schools to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain. Pupils are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is "right" and "wrong", all people living in England are subject to its law.
The Key Values are:
democracy
rule of law
individual liberty
mutual respect

Religious Education
Our curriculum intent for Religious Education reflects the purpose and aims of the National Curriculum by nurturing the spiritual, moral, social and cultural development of pupils and supporting wider community cohesion. Our RE planning is intended to offer a broad and rich RE curriculum; providing pupils with a variety of ways to explore religions, their community and unique personal development and wellbeing. The planning intends to provide a high quality, coherent and progressive experience of the subject, with scope for cross-curricular learning. Through each unit, children will know about and understand a range of religions. They will be able to identify, investigate and respond to a variety of ethical issues. We encourage pupils to understand the relevance of RE in today’s modern world and how it affects our lives.

Collective Worship
The Church of England vision for education is educating our children for ‘life in all its fullness’. At Kilmersdon Church School our Christian values are based on the teachings of Jesus Christ; Friendship, Perseverance, Trust, Peace, Forgiveness, and Hope. We focus on one of these each term. These Christian Values are explored through daily collective worship and through cross-curricular learning in class.
These values are embedded in the daily life of the school and have a significant impact on the spiritual, moral, social and cultural development of all members of the school community.
Collective worship, singing and celebration assemblies take place weekly. We use invitational prayer in our assemblies. We believe a daily act of worship provides an opportunity for children to create and participate in shared experiences of celebration, praise and thanksgiving.
We aim to enable pupils to reflect on our core Christian values and other values and beliefs to:
Provide aspirations for our children
Develop a sense of meaning, value and purpose
Celebrate difference and diversities
Encourage children’s natural sense of awe and wonder of God’s creation
Develop the qualities of curiosity, celebration and gratitude which form the foundation of worship
To develop a sense of community
Explore and reflect on the meaning and purpose of important life issues and give an opportunity to respond to questions relating to life and beliefs
Encourage participation and response
Encourage the development of spiritual and moral awareness
Explore a variety of forms of worship
Weekly Timetable
Acts of worship are led by SLT, local clergy, staff, pupils and guest speakers.
Monday: Whole School Worship reflecting on current values
Tuesday: Whole School Worship through song
Wednesday: Separate EYFS/KS1 and KS2 Worship reflecting on PSHE themes
Thursday: Whole School Worship reflecting on current values
Friday: Whole School Collective Worship and Celebration Assembly with parents
Local Church Links
At Kilmersdon Church School we are very lucky to have a strong relationship with St Peter and St Paul's Church. The School is only a short walk down the famous Jack and Jill hill to the church which enables the school to make full use of the facilities.
Our school families and the wider community regularly attend worship with our children for key events in the Christian calendar in the church.
You can find out more about St Peter and St Paul's church: Home - East Mendip Trinity Benefice

Welcome
Welcome to Kilmersdon Church School
'Ready, Respectful, Safe'
Welcome to Kilmersdon Church School — a small, caring rural school where every child is truly known, valued and celebrated.
At Kilmersdon, our children flourish within a close-knit community built on our core values of Peace, Perseverance, Forgiveness, Trust, Friendship and Hope. These values are not just words on a page; they guide everything we do, shaping the way we learn together, care for one another, and face challenges with confidence and kindness.
As a small school with mixed-age classes, we are proud of the strong family feel that defines our community. Our children learn to support one another, develop meaningful friendships across year groups, and grow in independence and responsibility. We believe this nurturing environment helps children develop a deep sense of belonging and an intrinsic happiness in who they are.
We hold high expectations for every child, encouraging curiosity, creativity and a love of learning. Through challenge and thoughtful support, we empower our pupils to believe in themselves, persevere when things are difficult, and take pride in their achievements. Compassion, respect and a sense of global responsibility are woven into daily school life, helping our children grow into thoughtful, caring citizens of the wider world.
Our beautiful rural setting provides rich opportunities for outdoor learning, reflection and exploration, and our strong Christian ethos underpins our commitment to inclusion, kindness and community.
We would be delighted to welcome you to Kilmersdon Church School and invite you to come and visit us. There is no better way to understand our school than to see the warmth, joy and determination of our children and staff for yourself.
We look forward to meeting you and sharing all that makes Kilmersdon such a special place to learn and grow.
Miss Dowley and Miss Baker
"That they may live life, life in all its fullness"
